## Claims
- [source-backed] For \(\mathfrak S_v=s_{i^j}\), the two proposed families are \(\{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\}\) and \(\{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}\), with \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\). [source-6, lines 14-33]
- [computed] For \((r,q,i,j)=(5,3,2,2)\), \(a=1,b=2,N=\binom31=3\), and the two families are \(F_1=(22,32,33)\) and \(F_2=(22,221,222)\). [artifact e03b87dfaac58fc8c68b65e28c061cd1ac2d9a04b2e72c5e80e07ffd2ad7d00f]
- [computed] In the \(3^5\)-box, the Schur-span module for shapes containing \(22\) has \(40\) ordered Schur columns. For \(F_1\), the complementary-column order is  
  \[
  \begin{gathered}
  221;2211,222,321;22111,2221,3211,322,331;\\
  22211,2222,32111,3221,3311,332;
  22221,32211,3222,33111,3321,333;\\
  22222,32221,33211,3322,3331;
  32222,33221,33311,3332;
  33222,33321,3333;33322,33331;33332;33333 .
  \end{gathered}
  \]
  The selected Pieri rows in the retained artifact order give a \(37\times37\) complementary minor of absolute determinant \(1\). [artifact e03b87dfaac58fc8c68b65e28c061cd1ac2d9a04b2e72c5e80e07ffd2ad7d00f]
- [computed] The separately formed direct-LR relation rows reduce integrally to the selected Pieri rows: the artifact retains, for each LR row, its integer coefficient vector in the fixed selected-row order. Hence the LR and selected-Pieri relation lattices agree for both \(F_1\) and \(F_2\). [artifact e03b87dfaac58fc8c68b65e28c061cd1ac2d9a04b2e72c5e80e07ffd2ad7d00f]
- [computed] The resulting Smith quotients are torsion-free of rank \(3\):
  \[
  J_{v_{5,5,4,8}}/\Lambda_+J_{v_{5,5,4,8}}\cong\mathbb Z^3,
  \]
  with respective bases given by the images of \(F_1\) and \(F_2\), subject to the standard integral box-model identification of this quotient. [artifact e03b87dfaac58fc8c68b65e28c061cd1ac2d9a04b2e72c5e80e07ffd2ad7d00f]

## Strategy
Use fixed Schur-column and Pieri-row orders; certify a unimodular complementary minor. Independently construct LR rows and retain their integral reductions to the selected Pieri lattice. The unimodular minor makes the quotient free on the three designated columns.

## Gaps
- The finite certificate requires independent audit of the two implementations and the retained reduction vectors.
- Minimality in the original integral ideal is conditional on the integral box-model and generation hypotheses; no uniform \(b=2\) result follows.

## Next
- Audit the artifact’s selected-row orders, minors, and LR reduction identities.
- Under the integral generation hypotheses, apply graded Nakayama to conclude irredundance of both three-element families.
